Description: Ten-digit number identifying every patient registered with NHS Scotland; encodes the date of birth (DDMMYY), two random digits, a sex digit (odd male, even female), and a Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: Printed on the NHS Scotland medical card, prescriptions, GP correspondence, hospital appointment letters, and the NHS Inform patient portal.

Description: Ten characters in the form YCCMMDDXYZK: Y is the last digit of the decade of birth; CC is a letter denoting the half-decade (A 1900–1904, B 1905–1909, etc.); MM is the month of birth (with +50 added for women); DD is the day; XYZ is a three-digit serial; and K is a check character (A–W) computed modulo 23.
Where to find it: Albanian biometric ID card (Letërnjoftim) and biometric passport issued by the General Directorate of Civil Status.

Personal identifier name endonym: رقم التعريف الوطني / Numéro d'Identification National (NIN)
Description: Eighteen-digit Numéro d'Identification National (NIN) issued by the Ministry of the Interior and printed on the biometric national identity card; encodes a sex marker, year of birth, the wilaya (province) and commune of the holder's civil-status registry, and a serial.
Where to find it: Algerian biometric National Identity Card (CNIBE) and biometric passport.

Personal identifier name endonym: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) Number / Tau IRD
Description: Eight- or nine-digit unique tax identifier issued by Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake); validated with a check digit computed using a weighted modular eleven algorithm. The companion National Health Index (NHI) number uses three letters and four digits.
Where to find it: IRD letters, payslips, KiwiSaver statements, the myIR online portal, and tax returns.

Description: Seven- or eight-digit number issued by the Registro Nacional de las Personas (RENAPER) to every person born in or naturalised in Argentina; serves as the unique civil identifier and is independent of the Clave Única de Identificación Tributaria (CUIT) and Clave Única de Identificación Laboral (CUIL) which prefix the DNI with sex/role digits and add a check digit.
Where to find it: Tarjeta DNI plastic card, passport, driving licence, voter rolls, and the Mi Argentina digital identity app.

Description: Ten-digit unique identifier assigned by the Public Services Number Service to every Armenian citizen and resident; introduced in 2012 to replace separate tax, social-insurance, and civil identifiers.
Where to find it: Armenian biometric identity card (անձնագիր) and biometric passport.

Description: Unique 16-digit number assigned by the Healthcare Identifiers Service to each person receiving healthcare in Australia, used to link records in My Health Record and other national digital health services.
Where to find it: Medicare online account, the My Health Record portal, hospital admission paperwork, and clinical correspondence.

Description: Eight- or nine-digit personal reference number issued by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) for tax and superannuation purposes; validated using a weighted check-digit algorithm (weights 1,4,3,7,5,8,6,9,10 modulo 11).
Where to find it: Notice of Assessment, payment summaries / income statements, the myGov / ATO online portal, and superannuation correspondence.

Description: Seven alphanumeric characters issued by the State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan; appears on the identity card and is used as a permanent personal identifier in all government databases.
Where to find it: Azerbaijani national identity card (Şəxsiyyət vəsiqəsi) and the ASAN e-government portal.

Description: Nine-digit Central Population Register (CPR) number assigned to every Bahraini citizen and resident at birth or upon receipt of a residence permit; the first two digits represent the year of registration and the remaining digits are a serial.
Where to find it: Bahraini Smart Card (Identity Card / CPR card) issued by the Information and eGovernment Authority (iGA), and the eKey single sign-on for government services.

Description: Originally 13 digits (or 17 digits including a four-digit year-of-birth prefix); the Smart NID introduced in 2016 standardises the number to 10 digits, randomly generated and issued by the Bangladesh Election Commission.
Where to find it: Smart NID card issued by the Bangladesh Election Commission, voter rolls, the Porichoy verification portal, and most government and banking services.

Description: Fourteen characters in the form GYYMMDDPRRRRC: G encodes sex and century of birth (1 male / 2 female 1800s; 3 male / 4 female 1900s; 5 male / 6 female 2000s; 7 male / 8 female 2100s); YYMMDD is the date of birth; P is a region letter (A Minsk City, B Minsk Region, C Brest, H Gomel, K Grodno, M Mogilev, P Vitebsk, E foreigner); RRRR is a serial; and C is a check digit.
Where to find it: Belarusian internal passport, biometric ID card, social-insurance card, and the единый портал электронных услуг (e-services portal).

Description: Eleven digits where the first six are the date of birth (YYMMDD), the next three are a serial ordering number (odd for men, even for women), and the last two are a Modulus-97 check digit.
Where to find it: Belgian electronic identity card (eID), SIS social-security card, passport, residence permit, and tax/health correspondence.

Description: Twelve-digit unique identification number issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) and linked to biometric (fingerprints, iris, photograph) and demographic data; first digit is never 0 or 1, and the number is validated with the Verhoeff check-digit algorithm.
Where to find it: Aadhaar letter / PVC card, e-Aadhaar PDF download, the mAadhaar app, DigiLocker, and the myAadhaar self-service portal.

Description: Six- to eight-digit number issued by the Servicio General de Identificación Personal (SEGIP) to every Bolivian citizen and foreign resident; duplicates between departments are disambiguated with a one- or two-letter “complemento” suffix.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad plastic card issued by SEGIP; also reused as the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) when registered as a taxpayer.

Country name endonym: Bosna i Hercegovina / Босна и Херцеговина
Personal identifier name endonym: Jedinstveni matični broj građana (JMBG) / Јединствени матични број грађана
Description: Thirteen digits in the shared Yugoslav-successor format DDMMYYY-RR-GGGC: seven-digit date of birth (last three digits of the year), two-digit registry / region code (10–19 for Bosnia and Herzegovina — 10 foreigners, 11 Banja Luka, 12 Bihać, 13 Doboj, 14 Goražde, 15 Livno, 16 Mostar, 17 Prijedor, 18 Sarajevo, 19 Tuzla), three digits combining sex and serial (000–499 male, 500–999 female), and a weighted Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: BiH personal identity card (lična karta / osobna iskaznica) and passport issued by the Agency for Identification Documents, Registers and Data Exchange (IDDEEA).

Description: Eleven digits in the format XXX.XXX.XXX-YY: nine sequential digits in which the ninth encodes the issuing tax region (1: DF/GO/MS/MT/TO; 2: AC/AM/AP/PA/RO/RR; 3: CE/MA/PI; 4: AL/PB/PE/RN; 5: BA/SE; 6: MG; 7: ES/RJ; 8: SP; 9: PR/SC; 0: RS), followed by two check digits computed modulo 11.
Where to find it: CPF card issued by the Receita Federal, the Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN) which now consolidates the CPF, RG and other identifiers, payslips, invoices, and the gov.br portal.

Personal identifier name endonym: Единен граждански номер (ЕГН) / Edinen grazhdanski nomer (EGN)
Description: Ten digits in the form YYMMDD-RRRGC: the first six encode the date of birth (with a month offset of +20 for 19th-century births and +40 for 21st-century births), three regional/serial digits, a gender digit (even for male, odd for female), and a weighted Modulus-10 check digit.
Where to find it: Bulgarian national identity card (Лична карта), passport, driving licence, and birth certificate.

Personal identifier name endonym: Social Insurance Number (SIN) / Numéro d'assurance sociale (NAS)
Description: Nine-digit number in XXX-XXX-XXX format with a final Luhn check digit. The leading digit identifies the region of original issuance: 1 = Atlantic provinces (NS, NB, NL, PE); 2–3 = Quebec; 4–5 = Ontario; 6 = Prairie provinces and Northern Canada (MB, SK, AB, NT, NU); 7 = Pacific (BC, YT); 8 = unused; 9 = temporary residents; 0 = unused.
Where to find it: Plastic / paper SIN card or confirmation letter from Service Canada, T4 / T5 / T4A slips, tax returns, payroll records, and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) “My Account” portal.

Description: Usually an eight-digit number (sometimes longer) printed on the data page of the biometric Czech passport issued by the Ministry of the Interior.
Where to find it: Czech passport (cestovní pas) issued by the Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic.

Description: Nine- or ten-digit number in the form YYXXDD/SSSC: YY is the last two digits of the year of birth; XX is the month of birth (01–12 for men, 51–62 for women, with +70 used when serial numbers run out); DD is the day; SSS is a serial number; and C is a check digit (omitted for people born before 1 January 1954). A ten-digit number must be divisible by 11.
Where to find it: Birth certificate, national ID card (občanský průkaz), driving licence, and health-insurance card.

Personal identifier name endonym: Rol Único Nacional (RUN) / Rol Único Tributario (RUT)
Personal identifier exonym English: Unique National Roll (RUN) / Unique Tax Roll (RUT)
Description: Seven- or eight-digit number followed by a hyphen and a verification character (a digit 0–9 or the letter K) computed modulo 11 using weights cycling 2 through 7. The RUN is the civil identifier carried by individuals; the RUT is the same number used for tax purposes by both natural and legal persons.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad (national ID card) issued by the Servicio de Registro Civil e Identificación, driving licence, passport, and tax filings with the Servicio de Impuestos Internos (SII).

Personal identifier name endonym: Número Único de Identificación Personal (NUIP) / Cédula de Ciudadanía (CC)
Personal identifier exonym English: Unique Personal Identification Number (NUIP) / Citizenship Card (CC)
Description: Numeric identifier issued by the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil. Citizens born after 2000 receive a NUIP starting at 1,000,000,000; legacy Cédulas de Ciudadanía are 8–10 digits. Children carry a Tarjeta de Identidad (TI) bearing the same NUIP that becomes the adult Cédula at 18.
Where to find it: Cédula de Ciudadanía (CC) / Cédula Digital, Tarjeta de Identidad for minors, passport, and the Registraduría's online verification service.

Description: Nine digits in the form P-NNNN-NNNN: P encodes the province of birth (1 San José, 2 Alajuela, 3 Cartago, 4 Heredia, 5 Guanacaste, 6 Puntarenas, 7 Limón; 8 and 9 reserved for naturalised citizens and special cases), followed by an eight-digit serial. The Cédula number underlies the NITE tax identifier.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad issued by the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) / Registro Civil; voter rolls and most government services.

Description: Thirteen-digit JMBG using the Yugoslav-successor scheme with two-digit registry / region codes 20–29 for Montenegro (e.g. 21 Podgorica, 23 Nikšić, 24 Cetinje, 25 Pljevlja, 26 Bijelo Polje, 27 Bar, 28 Herceg Novi, 29 Berane).
Where to find it: Montenegrin biometric ID card (Lična karta) and passport issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

Description: Eleven digits in the form YYMMDDCSSSC: six-digit date of birth, a one-digit century / nationality marker (0–5 for the 20th century, 6 for foreigners, 9 for the 21st century), three serial digits whose penultimate digit encodes sex (odd male, even female), and a final check digit.
Where to find it: Carné de Identidad plastic card issued by the Dirección de Identificación, Inmigración y Extranjería (DIIE) of the Ministry of the Interior.

Personal identifier name endonym: Rhif y Gwasanaeth Iechyd Gwladol (Rhif GIG)
Description: Ten-digit identifier in 3-3-4 format with a Modulus-11 check digit, shared with England and the Isle of Man and issued at birth or on first registration with a GP.
Where to find it: NHS Wales medical card, GP correspondence, prescriptions, hospital appointment letters, and the NHS Wales App.

Description: Passports issued before 13 December 2010 use the letter 'E' followed by six digits (e.g. E123456); biometric passports issued after that date use the letter 'K' followed by eight digits (e.g. K12345678).
Where to find it: Cyprus passport issued by the Civil Registry Department of the Ministry of the Interior.

Description: Thirteen digits in the format YYMMDD-SBBBBNC: YYMMDD is the date of birth; S encodes century and sex (1 male / 2 female born 1900–1999; 3 male / 4 female born 2000–2099; 5 male / 6 female for foreign nationals born 1900–1999; 7 male / 8 female for foreign nationals born 2000–2099; 9/0 used pre-1900); BBBB is a region-of-birth and serial code; N is a tiebreaker digit; and C is a weighted Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: Korean Resident Registration Card (주민등록증), driving licence, passport, and government online services such as Government24 (정부24) and Hometax.

Description: Ten-digit code in the form DDMMYY-SSSC: the first six digits encode the date of birth, the next three are a serial number whose final digit encodes sex (odd for men, even for women), and the last is a Modulus-11 check digit (no longer mandatory for validation of new CPR numbers).
Where to find it: Danish health insurance card (sundhedskort), national ID, driving licence, passport, and most official correspondence.

Description: Lifelong federal health-insurance identifier: one random uppercase letter followed by eight random digits and a Luhn check digit, carried on the electronic health card (elektronische Gesundheitskarte, eGK).
Where to find it: German electronic health insurance card (eGK), insurer correspondence, and prescriptions.

Personal identifier name endonym: Cédula de Identidad (CI) / Cédula de Ciudadanía
Description: Ten digits: the first two encode the province of issuance (01–24, with 30 for naturalised citizens and 50 for the diplomatic register); the third digit is between 0 and 5 for individuals; the next six are a serial; and the tenth is a Modulus-10 check digit computed with the cycling Luhn-style weights 2,1.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad plastic card issued by the Dirección General de Registro Civil, Identificación y Cedulación, and the Cédula Digital wallet.

Description: Eleven digits in the form GYYMMDDSSSC: G encodes sex and century of birth (1–2 for the 19th century, 3–4 for the 20th, 5–6 for the 21st, with odd numbers male and even female); YYMMDD is the date of birth; SSS is a serial number; and C is a Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: Estonian ID card (ID-kaart), passport, residence permit, driving licence, and digital signing services such as Smart-ID and Mobiil-ID.

Description: Ten-digit lifelong identifier created under the 2014 Health Identifiers Act and operated by the Health Service Executive (HSE) to uniquely identify every person using a health or social care service in Ireland.
Where to find it: HSE correspondence, hospital and GP appointment letters, the National Shared Care Record, and patient-facing portals.

Description: Nine digits in the format NNNNNNNN-N: eight sequential digits and a final check digit computed modulo 10. The DUI replaced the legacy Cédula de Identidad Personal, electoral card, and other identifiers in 2001.
Where to find it: DUI plastic card issued by the Registro Nacional de las Personas Naturales (RNPN); voter rolls and most government services.

Personal identifier exonym English: Dematerialised Securities System (DSS) Investor Share Code
Description: Ten-digit investor identifier linked to personal details (name, identity-card number, passport number, tax registration number); the investor share is the account record held in the DSS operated by the Hellenic Central Securities Depository (ATHEXCSD).
Where to find it: Account statements and confirmations issued by the Hellenic Central Securities Depository (ATHEXCSD) and by the investor's appointed operator (broker or bank).

Description: Ten-digit number in 3-3-4 format with a Modulus-11 check digit, allocated through the Personal Demographics Service and used as the key patient identifier across the English NHS.
Where to find it: NHS medical card, GP correspondence, prescriptions, hospital letters, the NHS App and NHS login, and online services such as patient.nhs.uk.

Personal identifier name endonym: Código de Identificación Fiscal (CIF) / Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF)
Description: Nine characters: eight digits plus a control letter (the letters I, Ñ, O, and U are not used). Example: 99111222M. For Spanish citizens the NIF equals the DNI; foreign residents use the NIE (leading letter X, Y, or Z). Since 2008 the CIF form is reserved for legal entities, while NIF designates natural persons.
Where to find it: Spanish national identity card (DNI), the residence card (NIE) for foreign residents, the driving licence, and the social security card.

Description: Individual health card issued by the autonomous regional health administrations and INGESA, linked to the unique CIP-SNS code (Código de Identificación Personal del Sistema Nacional de Salud) and valid throughout Spain's National Health System.
Where to find it: Plastic Tarjeta Sanitaria Individual card issued by the regional health service, prescriptions, hospital identity bands, and the Mi Carpeta Ciudadana portal.

Description: Twelve-digit Fayda Identity Number (FIN) assigned by the National ID Programme (NIDP) on the Modular Open-Source Identity Platform (MOSIP); linked to fingerprint and iris biometrics and rolled out from 2023 as a universal digital identifier replacing the older Kebele ID.
Where to find it: Fayda National ID card and the Fayda e-ID app issued by the National ID Programme of Ethiopia.

Description: Thirteen-digit “meaningful” code plus a two-digit check key, managed by INSEE in the Répertoire National d'Identification des Personnes Physiques (RNIPP). It encodes sex (1 male, 2 female), year and month of birth, INSEE département and commune of birth, and a serial number; commonly called the French social security number.
Where to find it: Carte Vitale health insurance card, payslips, tax forms, the Ameli health portal, France Connect, and pension correspondence.

Description: Personal Identification Number printed on the Ghana Card in the format GHA-NNNNNNNNN-X: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code GHA, nine random digits, and a check character. Issued by the National Identification Authority (NIA) under the 2008 National Identification Authority Act.
Where to find it: Ghana Card (national biometric ID card) issued by the National Identification Authority; required for SIM-card registration, banking (linked to the Tax Identification Number), passport applications, and the electoral roll.

Description: Thirteen-digit Código Único de Identificación (CUI) in the form NNNN-NNNNN-NNNN: a four-digit serial within the local registry, a five-digit running serial including a check digit, and a four-digit municipality / department code.
Where to find it: DPI plastic card issued by the Registro Nacional de las Personas (RENAP); voter rolls.

Description: Thirteen digits in the format DDDD-YYYY-NNNNN: DDDD encodes the department and municipality of birth, YYYY is the year of birth, and NNNNN is a serial within that year and locality.
Where to find it: DNI plastic card issued by the Registro Nacional de las Personas (RNP); voter rolls and most government services.

Description: Eleven-digit code: ten randomly assigned digits with no information about the holder, followed by an ISO 7064 MOD 11,10 check digit. OIB is unique, unchangeable, and unrepeatable, and is the permanent identification code of every Croatian citizen and every legal person headquartered in Croatia.
Where to find it: Croatian national identity card (Osobna iskaznica), passport, driving licence, tax records (Porezna uprava lookup), and most personal documents.

Description: Sixteen digits in the form PPRRCCDDMMYYNNNN: PP is the province code, RR is the regency/city (kabupaten/kota) code, CC is the sub-district (kecamatan) code, DDMMYY is the date of birth (with +40 added to the day for women), and NNNN is a serial number issued by the local civil-registration office.
Where to find it: Kartu Tanda Penduduk elektronik (KTP-el) issued by the Directorate General of Population and Civil Registration (Dukcapil), Kartu Keluarga (family card), tax records, and the Identitas Kependudukan Digital (IKD) app.

Personal identifier name endonym: شماره ملی (Shomāreh Mellī) / کد ملی (Kod Mellī)
Description: Ten digits where the first three encode the city or shahrestan of registration, the next six are a serial number, and the final digit is a check digit computed by weighted multiplication (10,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2) modulo 11 (a remainder of 0 or 1 maps directly, otherwise C = 11 − remainder).
Where to find it: Iranian National Identity Card (کارت ملی, Kart-e Mellī), the civil birth booklet (شناسنامه, Shenāsnāmeh), and the My Iran (دولت همراه) services portal.

Description: Twelve-digit Iraqi National Card number issued by the General Directorate of Nationality from 2015; consolidates the older Civil Status Identity Card (Bitāqat al-Aḥwāl al-Madaniyya) and Nationality Certificate (Shahādat al-Jinsiyya) into a single biometric card.
Where to find it: Unified National Card (البطاقة الوطنية الموحدة) issued by the General Directorate of Nationality of the Ministry of Interior.

Description: Ten-digit identifier in the form DDMMYY-RRCC: the first six digits are the date of birth, the next two are a random serial, then a Modulus-11 check digit, and a final digit denoting the century of birth (9 for 19th, 0 for 20th, 1 for 21st).
Where to find it: Icelandic National Registry (Þjóðskrá Íslands) record, national ID card, passport, driving licence, and all official forms and contracts.

Description: Sixteen-character alphanumeric code issued by the Agenzia delle Entrate, derived from surname (3 letters), given name (3 letters), date of birth and sex (5 alphanumeric characters with day +40 for women), place of birth (4-character Belfiore code), and a final check letter. Example: RSSMRA62B25E205Y.
Where to find it: Codice Fiscale paper card or Tessera Sanitaria (national health-service card), which carries the fiscal code on a magnetic stripe.

Description: Nine-digit unique number issued by Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ) to every Jamaican citizen, resident, and registered organisation; serves as the de facto national identifier pending the rollout of the National Identification System (NIDS).
Where to find it: TRN card issued by Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ); driving licence; bank-account opening; SIM-card registration.

Description: Ten-digit unique identifier issued by the Civil Status and Passport Department to every Jordanian citizen and to many residents; the first digit encodes citizenship class (typically 9 for Jordanian citizens) and the remaining digits include a date-derived component and a serial.
Where to find it: Jordanian Smart ID card and family booklet (دفتر العائلة) issued by the Civil Status and Passport Department; the Sanad e-government app.

Personal identifier name endonym: Жеке сәйкестендіру нөмірі (ЖСН) / Индивидуальный идентификационный номер (ИИН)
Description: Twelve digits in the form YYMMDDSGNNNNC: YYMMDD is the date of birth; S encodes century and sex (1 male / 2 female 1800s; 3 male / 4 female 1900s; 5 male / 6 female 2000s); G is a serial / generation indicator; NNNN is a serial; and C is a weighted Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: Kazakh ID card (Жеке куәлік), passport, and the eGov.kz portal.

Description: Eight-digit unique serial number issued by the National Registration Bureau to every Kenyan citizen from the age of 18. The companion Huduma Namba — a parallel ten-digit identifier introduced under 2019 amendments — was launched as a unified register but its rollout has been suspended since the 2021 High Court ruling.
Where to find it: Kenyan National ID Card (Kitambulisho) issued by the National Registration Bureau under the Ministry of Interior, the eCitizen portal, and the suspended Huduma Namba registration card.

Description: Twelve digits in the form CYYMMDDSSSSC: a leading century digit (2 = 1900–1999, 3 = 2000+), six-digit date of birth, four-digit serial, and a final check digit. Issued by the Public Authority for Civil Information (PACI).
Where to find it: Kuwait Civil ID (البطاقة المدنية), the Kuwait Mobile ID app, and the SAHEL e-government app.

Description: Eleven digits in the form DDMMYY-CZZZZ: the first six are the date of birth, C is the century sign (0 for 19th century, 1 for 20th, 2 for 21st), ZZZZ is a serial number, and the last digit is a check digit.
Where to find it: Latvian eID card, passport, driving licence, and the official Latvija.lv portal.

Personal identifier name endonym: Matricule National (numéro d'identification national) / Nationale Identifikationsnummer
Description: Thirteen digits in the form YYYYMMDDSSSCC: eight-digit date of birth, three-digit serial, and two check digits (the first computed with the Luhn algorithm, the second with the Verhoeff algorithm).
Where to find it: Luxembourg national identity card (Carte d'identité), social-security card (Carte de sécurité sociale), passport, and the MyGuichet.lu portal.

Description: Combination of 2 letters and 8 numbers, for example ID022143586. The number is regenerated on each renewal of the identity card.
Where to find it: Liechtenstein national identity card (Identitätskarte) issued by the Office of Civil Affairs (Amt für Zivilstandswesen).

Description: Combination of 1 letter and 5 numbers, for example R00536.
Where to find it: Liechtenstein passport (Reisepass) issued by the Office of Civil Affairs.

Description: Eleven digits in the form GYYMMDDNNNC: G encodes sex and century of birth (3/5 for men born in the 20th/21st century, 4/6 for women born in the 20th/21st century); YYMMDD is the date of birth; NNN is a serial number; and C is a Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: Lithuanian ID card (Asmens tapatybės kortelė), passport, driving licence, residence permit, and most government correspondence.

Description: Eight-digit passport-document number printed on the Lithuanian passport (the same document number form is also used on the national ID card).
Where to find it: Lithuanian passport (Pasas) and national ID card issued by the Migration Department.

Description: Composite identifier issued by the General Directorate of Personal Status (Mudīriyyat al-Aḥwāl ash-Shakhṣiyya) within the Ministry of Interior; quotes a place of registration (“matn as-sijill” — typically a village or town civil register) and a serial / page number within that local register.
Where to find it: Lebanese ikhrāj al-qaid (family extract / civil-status extract), Hawiyya identity card, and biometric passport.

Description: Eleven digits in the form X-YYMMDD-ZZZC: X encodes century and sex (1 male / 2 female born 1900–1999; 3 male / 4 female born 1800–1899; 5 male / 6 female born 2000–2099); YYMMDD is the date of birth; ZZZ is a serial number; and C is a weighted Modulus-11 check digit. Because of constitutional privacy rules the personal identification number is stored separately from the eID and is generally not printed on the card.
Where to find it: Issued by the Belügyminisztérium; appears on the official hatósági bizonyítvány a személyazonosító jelről (personal-identification-number certificate), the historical address card (lakcímkártya), the social-security TAJ card, and government records.

Description: Twelve digits in the format YYMMDD-PB-###G: YYMMDD is the date of birth; PB is the place-of-birth code (states 01–16 for those born in Malaysia, or country codes 60–85 for those born abroad); ### is a serial; and G is a sex digit (odd male, even female).
Where to find it: MyKad smart card issued by the National Registration Department (Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara, JPN), MyDigital ID app, driving licence, passport.

Description: Eight characters: seven digits and a trailing letter (M, G, A, P, L, H, B, or Z). The letter encodes the geographic origin and registration context: A foreigner with eRes Card; B Maltese births registered in the 1800s; G Gozitan births registered in the 1900s; H Gozitan births registered in the 2000s; L Maltese births registered in the 2000s; M Maltese births registered in the 1900s; P Maltese citizens registered without an original birth certificate from their country of birth; Z Gozitan births registered in the 1800s.
Where to find it: Maltese national identity card (Karta tal-Identità) issued by Identity Malta.

Description: Seven numerical digits, issued by Identity Malta (formerly the Civil Registration Directorate).
Where to find it: Maltese passport (Passaport) issued by Identity Malta.

Personal identifier name endonym: Carte Nationale d'Identité Électronique (CNIE) / البطاقة الوطنية للتعريف الإلكترونية
Description: Identity-card number consisting of one or two prefix letters (encoding the province of issuance) followed by six or seven digits — for example G123456 or AB123456. Issued by the Direction Générale de la Sûreté Nationale (DGSN).
Where to find it: Moroccan electronic National Identity Card (CNIE) issued by the General Directorate of National Security; required for civil, electoral, banking, and administrative procedures.

Personal identifier name endonym: Clave Única de Registro de Población (CURP)
Description: Eighteen characters: four letters drawn from the holder's first surname, second surname, and given name; six digits for date of birth (YYMMDD); one letter for sex (H male, M female); two letters for the federative entity of birth (or NE if born abroad); three consonants taken from inside the surnames and given name; one alphanumeric “homonym” character (a letter for births before 2000, a digit thereafter); and a final check digit computed modulo 10.
Where to find it: CURP printout from gob.mx, INE/IFE voter ID card, Mexican passport, the acta de nacimiento (birth certificate), and the RFC tax record which incorporates the CURP.

Description: Fourteen digits in the form C-YYMMDD-GG-SSSS-S: C encodes the century (2 for the 20th century, 3 for the 21st); YYMMDD is the date of birth; GG is the governorate of birth (88 indicates born abroad); SSSS is a serial in which the penultimate digit encodes sex (odd male, even female); and the final digit is a check digit.
Where to find it: Egyptian National Identity Card (بطاقة الرقم القومي) issued by the Civil Status Sector of the Ministry of Interior; mandatory for adult citizens since 2008.

Description: Thirteen digits assigned by the Public Services Agency (Agenția Servicii Publice) and recorded in the State Register of Population. The leading digit identifies the entity class (0 for natural persons, 1 for legal entities), followed by serial digits and a final check digit.
Where to find it: Moldovan ID card (buletin de identitate), passport, driving licence, and the MPass / MSign e-government services.

Description: Ten characters in the form LL-YYMMDD-NNN-C: two Cyrillic letters encoding the aimag or city of registration (e.g. ОЛ for Ulaanbaatar); six digits for date of birth (YYMMDD); a three-digit serial whose parity encodes sex (odd male, even female); and a final check digit.
Where to find it: Mongolian Citizen Identity Card (Иргэний үнэмлэх) issued by the General Authority for State Registration.

Personal identifier name endonym: နိုင်ငံသား မှတ်ပုံတင် (Naingngantha Hmat Pon Tin)
Description: Composite identifier in the form RR/TTT(C)NNNNNN: RR is a two-digit regional code; TTT is a township abbreviation in Burmese script; (C) is a one-letter citizenship status indicator in parentheses (N full citizen, E associate citizen, T naturalised citizen, A foreign resident); and NNNNNN is a six-digit serial.
Where to find it: National Registration Card (NRC) — also called the Citizenship Scrutiny Card (CSC) — issued by the General Administration Department of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Description: Nine-digit citizen service number issued through the Personal Records Database (Basisregistratie Personen, BRP); introduced in 2007, validated with a variant of the eleven-test (Luhn-style) algorithm, and required for all dealings with the Dutch government.
Where to find it: Dutch passport, identity card (Nederlandse identiteitskaart), driving licence, payslips, tax correspondence, and the DigiD-protected MijnOverheid portal.

Description: Nine characters: positions 1 and 2 are uppercase letters [A-Z] except O; positions 3–8 are alphanumeric [A-Z][0-9] except the letter O; position 9 is a digit [0-9]. The character O is disallowed (to avoid confusion with 0), but the digit 0 is allowed.
Where to find it: Dutch national identity card (Nederlandse identiteitskaart), printed on the front of the card and in the machine-readable zone.

Description: Nine characters: positions 1 and 2 are uppercase letters [A-Z] except O; positions 3–8 are alphanumeric [A-Z][0-9] except O; position 9 is a digit [0-9].
Where to find it: Dutch passport (Nederlands paspoort), printed on the data page and in the machine-readable zone.

Description: Ten- or eleven-digit National Identity Number issued by the Department of National ID and Civil Registration under the 2019 National Identity Card Programme; linked to biometric data (fingerprints, iris, photograph). The smart card is gradually replacing the older Nāgariktā (citizenship certificate).
Where to find it: Smart National Identity Card (Rāṣṭriya Parichaya-patra) issued by the Department of National ID and Civil Registration of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Description: Eleven-digit number randomly assigned by the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) under the 2007 NIMC Act and linked to ten biometric fingerprints, a facial photograph, and demographic data; used as the unique citizen and resident identifier.
Where to find it: NIN slip, National e-ID card, and the NIMC Mobile ID app; required for SIM-card registration, banking (BVN), passports, and the JAMB examination.

Personal identifier name endonym: 個人番号 (Kojin Bangō) / マイナンバー (My Number)
Description: Twelve-digit number assigned to each resident under the 2015 Social Security and Tax Number System (Act on the Use of Numbers to Identify a Specific Individual), with a final check digit computed via weighted multiplication and Modulus-11. The number is permanent and carried for a person's lifetime.
Where to find it: My Number Card (マイナンバーカード) issued by municipal governments, the older Notification Card (通知カード), and tax / employment / pension paperwork.

Description: Eleven digits where the first six are the date of birth (DDMMYY) and the next three are a personal/serial number — odd for males, even for females. The final two digits are check digits computed using a weighted Modulus-11.
Where to find it: Norwegian passport, national ID card, driving licence, bank cards, payslips, and the Altinn government portal.

Description: Ten-digit identifier in the same 3-3-4 format as the NHS number, drawn from a reserved range (320 000 001 to 399 999 999) and used across Health and Social Care Northern Ireland (HSCNI).
Where to find it: HSCNI medical card, GP correspondence, hospital appointment letters, and prescriptions across Northern Ireland.

Description: Eight-digit civil number issued by the Royal Oman Police Directorate General of Civil Status; printed on the smart Resident Card together with a separate card serial number.
Where to find it: Omani Resident Card (بطاقة الهوية) — Resident Card for non-Omanis — required for banking, employment, and government services.

Description: Ten digits in the form AAACDDMMYY: AAA is a three-digit serial number assigned by the social insurance carrier; C is a check digit computed with weights 3,7,9,5,8,4,2,1,6 modulo 11 (a remainder of 10 yields a fresh AAA); and DDMMYY is the date of birth.
Where to find it: Austrian e-card (electronic health-insurance card), payslips, tax forms, FinanzOnline, and pension correspondence.

Description: Thirteen digits in the format AAAAA-BBBBBBB-G: the first five digits encode province / division / district / tehsil of permanent address, the next seven are a family / individual serial within that registration unit, and the final digit is a gender digit (odd male, even female).
Where to find it: CNIC plastic card or Smart NIC issued by the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA), Pak-Identity online portal, passport, and SIM-card registration.

Description: Format Province-Tomo-Asiento: a province / origin prefix (1–13 for Panamanian provinces and indigenous comarcas; PE for born in Panamá Este; E for naturalised foreigners; N for children of foreigners born in Panama) followed by “tomo” (volume) and “asiento” (registry entry) numbers — for example 8-123-456.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad Personal issued by the Tribunal Electoral; voter rolls; banking and tax records.

Description: Up to seven-digit serial number assigned by the Departamento de Identificaciones of the Policía Nacional and held for life; the same number underlies the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) tax identifier, extended with a verification digit.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad Civil issued by the Policía Nacional, voter rolls (TSJE), and SET tax records.

Description: Eight-digit number issued by the Registro Nacional de Identificación y Estado Civil (RENIEC), with an additional verification digit printed alongside it; the same DNI is used by minors (DNI azul) and adults (DNI electrónico / DNIe) and underlies the universal voter roll.
Where to find it: DNI card or DNI electrónico (DNIe) issued by RENIEC, passport, and the ID Perú digital identity app.

Description: Twelve-digit, randomly generated, permanent number issued by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) under the 2018 Philippine Identification System Act (RA 11055). The plastic PhilID and ePhilID carry a derived sixteen-digit PhilSys Card Number (PCN) so the underlying PSN can be revoked and re-issued if compromised.
Where to find it: PhilID physical card, ePhilID printout, and the PhilSys digital national ID app.

Description: Ten numeric digits with a Modulus-11 weighted check digit, used by investment firms and the tax administration to identify a person or organisation for tax purposes.
Where to find it: NIP confirmation document, tax forms (PIT, including the PIT-8 issued by investment firms), invoices, and contracts.

Description: Eleven numeric digits in the form YYMMDDSSSSC: the date of birth (with month offset +20 for the 2000s, +40 for the 2100s, +60 for the 2200s, −20 for the 1800s), four serial digits (the penultimate digit encodes sex — odd male, even female), and a weighted Modulus-10 check digit. The PESEL is assigned shortly after birth and is permanent.
Where to find it: Polish ID card (dowód osobisty), passport, driving licence, birth certificate, and the obywatel.gov.pl portal.

Description: Nine digits, the first eight sequential and the ninth a check digit. The leading digit encodes the entity type: 1–3 individuals; 45 non-residents earning Portuguese income subject to withholding; 5 resident legal entities; 6 public administration; 70/74/75 indivisible estates; 71 non-resident entities subject to definitive withholding; 72 investment funds; 77 NIFs allocated by the tax authority; 78 non-residents in the VAT refund scheme; 79 special cases; 8 sole traders (legacy); 90/91 condominiums, irregular societies, undivided inheritances; 98 non-residents without permanent establishment; 99 civil societies without legal personality.
Where to find it: Portuguese Cartão de Cidadão (which carries the NIF alongside the civil identification number), tax invoices, employer/contract documents, and the Portal das Finanças.

Description: Uniform optical-model passport identified by one letter and six digits — position 1 is a letter [A-Z] and positions 2–6 are digits [0-9].
Where to find it: Portuguese passport, printed on the data page and in the machine-readable zone.

Description: Eleven-digit Qatari ID (QID): a leading century-of-birth digit (2 = 1900–1999, 3 = 2000+), two digits for year of birth, three digits for the ISO-style country-of-nationality code (634 for Qatar), and a five-digit serial.
Where to find it: Qatari ID (QID) card issued by the Ministry of Interior General Directorate of Passports, Hukoomi (e-government portal), and the Metrash2 app.

Description: Eleven digits in the form XXX-NNNNNNN-X: a three-digit municipal / district code assigned by the Junta Central Electoral, a seven-digit serial, and a Luhn check digit.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad y Electoral issued by the Junta Central Electoral (JCE), used as both the civil identity document and the voter registration.

Description: Thirteen digits: a leading sex/century digit (1 male 1900–1999, 2 female 1900–1999, 3 male 1800–1899, 4 female 1800–1899, 5 male 2000+, 6 female 2000+, 7 male resident, 8 female resident, 9 foreign citizen); date of birth (YYMMDD); two-digit county code (01–52, or 99 for non-Romanians, or 4 followed by a Bucharest sector number); a three-digit serial number; and a check digit computed by weighted multiplication with the constant 279146358279 modulo 11 (remainder 10 maps to 1).
Where to find it: Romanian Birth Certificate, Identity Card (Carte de Identitate), and Driving Licence.

Description: Eight characters: positions 1 and 2 are letters [A-Z] and positions 3–8 are digits [0-9].
Where to find it: Romanian passport (Paşaport), printed on the data page.

Personal identifier name endonym: Страховой номер индивидуального лицевого счёта (СНИЛС, SNILS)
Personal identifier exonym English: Insurance Number of Individual Personal Account (SNILS)
Description: Eleven digits in the format XXX-XXX-XXX YY: nine digits identify the account holder and the last two digits are a checksum computed with weights 9,8,…,1 (sum modulo 101; results of 100 or 101 map to 00).
Where to find it: Green SNILS card (zelyonaya kartochka) issued by the Pension Fund of Russia (since 2019, by the Social Fund), payslips, pension statements, and the Gosuslugi portal; the companion ИНН (INN) tax number is twelve digits for individuals.

Description: Eleven-digit unique personal identifier assigned by the Public Service Development Agency (PSDA) and used in every government register; the first two digits encode the issuing region (district code) and the remaining digits include a serial and a check digit.
Where to find it: Georgian biometric ID card (პირადობის მოწმობა) and passport issued by the Public Service Development Agency; the my.gov.ge portal.

Description: Ten digits beginning with 1 for Saudi citizens or 2 for foreign residents (the Iqama number), followed by eight serial digits and a final Luhn-style check digit; issued and managed by the General Directorate of Civil Status (Ahwal Madaniyyah) under the Ministry of Interior.
Where to find it: National Identity Card (بطاقة الهوية الوطنية) or Iqama (إقامة) residency permit, and the Absher and Tawakkalna government apps.

Personal identifier name endonym: AHV-Nummer / Numéro AVS / Numero AVS / Numer AVS
Description: Thirteen digits in the form 756.XXXX.XXXX.XC: 756 is the ISO 3166-1 numeric code for Switzerland, followed by nine random digits, with a final EAN-13 (Modulus-10) check digit. Issued by the Central Compensation Office (CCO / ZAS) and reused since 2008 as a general administrative identifier in addition to the social-insurance role.
Where to find it: AHV/AVS insurance card, electronic health-insurance card, tax records, pension correspondence, and the SwissID e-government portal.

Personal identifier name endonym: Единствен матичен број на граѓанинот (ЕМБГ) / Edinstven matičen broj na graǵaninot (EMBG)
Description: Thirteen-digit identifier in the Yugoslav-successor JMBG family with two-digit registry / region codes 40–49 for North Macedonia (e.g. 41 Bitola, 42 Kumanovo, 43 Ohrid, 44 Prilep, 45 Skopje, 46 Strumica, 47 Tetovo, 48 Veles, 49 Štip). Format: DDMMYYY-RR-GGGC with a weighted Modulus-11 check digit.
Where to find it: Macedonian Personal ID card (Лична карта) and passport issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

Description: One prefix letter (S or T for citizens / PRs depending on year of issuance; F or G for foreigners on long-term passes depending on year; M for foreigners issued from 1 January 2022), seven digits, and a checksum letter. S/F use weights 2,7,6,5,4,3,2 on the seven digits and look up the result in fixed alphabets; T/G use the same with a +4 offset on the sum; M uses a different reversed alphabet.
Where to find it: NRIC / Identity Card (pink for citizens, blue for PRs) issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), Long-Term Pass card, and the Singpass digital ID app.

Description: Thirteen digits in the form DDMMYYY-RR-GGGC: seven-digit date of birth (last three digits of the year), a two-digit registry/republic code (50/59 for Slovenia after 18 February 1999, with 10–19 Bosnia and Herzegovina, 20–29 Montenegro, 30–39 Croatia, 40–49 Macedonia, 70–79 Serbia, 80–89 Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, 90–99 Kosovo for pre-1999 issuance), three digits combining sex and serial number (000–499 male, 500–999 female), and a weighted Modulus-11 check digit defined in Article 4 of the Regulation on the way of assigning the personal identification number.
Where to find it: Slovenian Personal Identity Card (Osebna izkaznica), passport, birth certificate, and tax records.

Description: Nine characters in the format XXNNNNNNN — two block letters followed by seven digits — with a ten-year validity.
Where to find it: Slovak passport (Cestovný pas); citizens who hold two passports simultaneously will only find the document number on the first one.

Description: Ten-digit code in the form YYMMDDCCCX: the first six digits are the date of birth (with month offset of +50 for women, so MM is 01–12 for men and 51–62 for women), CCC is a serial number distinguishing persons born on the same date, and X is a check digit such that the entire number is divisible by 11.
Where to find it: Birth certificate (rodný list), national ID card (občiansky preukaz), driving licence, and other personal documents.

Country name endonym: South Africa / Suid-Afrika / iRiphabhuliki yaseNingizimu Afrika
Description: Thirteen digits in the format YYMMDDSSSSCAZ: YYMMDD is the date of birth; SSSS is a sex serial (0000–4999 female, 5000–9999 male); C is citizenship status at birth (0 South African citizen, 1 permanent resident); A is a legacy “race” indicator now fixed at 8 or 9; and Z is a Luhn check digit.
Where to find it: Smart ID Card or Green Barcoded ID Book issued by the Department of Home Affairs (DHA), driving licence, and passport.

Personal identifier name endonym: Јединствени матични број грађана (ЈМБГ) / Jedinstveni matični broj građana (JMBG)
Description: Thirteen digits in the form DDMMYYY-RR-GGGC: seven-digit date of birth (last three digits of the year), two-digit registry / republic code for the region of birth (Serbia 70–79; Vojvodina 80–89; Kosovo 90–99 for pre-1999 issuance; specific district codes within each), three digits combining sex and serial (000–499 male, 500–999 female), and a weighted Modulus-11 check digit. The same JMBG scheme is shared across the former Yugoslav republics.
Where to find it: Lična karta (national ID card) and pasoš (passport) issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MUP), driving licence, and tax records.

Personal identifier name endonym: ජාතික හැඳුනුම්පත (Jātika Handunumpata) / தேசிய அடையாள அட்டை
Description: Two formats coexist. Legacy NICs use nine digits and a letter (e.g. 200123456V): the first two digits are the last two of the year of birth, the next three are the day-of-year (+500 added for women), then a four-digit serial, and a verification character (V for citizens, X for non-citizens). The 2016 e-NIC uses twelve digits, expanding year of birth to four digits and dropping the trailing letter.
Where to find it: National Identity Card (NIC) issued by the Department for Registration of Persons.

Description: Eleven characters of the form DDMMYYCZZZQ: DDMMYY is the date of birth, C is the century sign (+ for 1800–1899, - for 1900–1999, A for 2000–2099), ZZZ is the individual number (odd for males and even for females; for people born in Finland the range is 002–899), and Q is the check character (a digit or letter from a defined alphabet). Example: 311280-888Y.
Where to find it: Finnish ID card, passport, residence permit, driving licence, and the Suomi.fi portal.

Description: National identification number issued by Skatteverket since 1947, twelve digits CCYYMMDDZZZQ in automated data (or ten digits when the century is implicit). CCYYMMDD is the date of birth, ZZZ is the individual serial number whose third digit is odd for males and even for females, and Q is a Luhn check digit.
Where to find it: Passports, national ID cards, driving licences, health-care cards, payslips, and tax correspondence; held by the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket).

Personal identifier name endonym: 國民身分證統一編號 (Guómín Shēnfènzhèng Tǒngyī Biānhào)
Description: One letter (A–Z, indicating the place of household registration; e.g. A = Taipei City, B = Taichung City, C = Keelung City) followed by nine digits: a sex digit (1 male, 2 female), seven serial digits, and a final check digit. The leading letter is converted to two digits via a lookup table, then a weighted sum modulo 10 yields the check digit.
Where to find it: National Identification Card (中華民國國民身分證) issued by the Household Registration Office of the Ministry of the Interior, household registration transcript (戶籍謄本), and the My Data (我的E政府) portal.

Description: Twenty-digit number assigned by the National Identification Authority (NIDA) to every Tanzanian citizen and long-term resident; encodes the year and country of birth, region and district of registration, and a serial.
Where to find it: National ID card (Kitambulisho cha Taifa) issued by NIDA; required for SIM-card registration, banking, employment, and most government services.

Personal identifier name endonym: เลขประจำตัวประชาชน (Lek Prajam Tua Prachāchon)
Description: Thirteen digits in the form X-XXXX-XXXXX-XX-X. The first digit classifies the type of registration (1 Thai citizens born after 1 January 1984 and registered within the deadline; 2 Thais registered late; 3 Thais already in the registry before 1984; 4 those who were registered as Thai citizens after 1984; 5 added later to the registry; 6–7 foreign residents; 8 newly naturalised; 0 temporary identification). The following digits encode the registration district and a serial; the last digit is a Modulus-11 check digit (sum of digits 1–12 multiplied by weights 13–2, mod 11, then 11 minus the remainder mod 10).
Where to find it: Smart ID Card (บัตรประจำตัวประชาชน) issued by the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA, กรมการปกครอง), Thai house registration (ทะเบียนบ้าน), and the ThaID government identity app.

Personal identifier name endonym: بطاقة التعريف الوطنية / Carte d'Identité Nationale (CIN)
Description: Eight-digit unique identifier assigned by the Ministry of the Interior at age 18 (or earlier for travel); printed on the CIN, embossed on banking and tax records, and reused as the personal portion of the matricule fiscal (tax registration).
Where to find it: Carte d'Identité Nationale (بطاقة التعريف الوطنية) issued by the Ministry of the Interior; passport.

Description: Eleven digits that can never start with 0; the tenth digit equals ((sum of digits 1,3,5,7,9 × 7) − (sum of digits 2,4,6,8)) mod 10, and the eleventh equals (sum of the first ten digits) mod 10. Issued by the General Directorate of Civil Registration and Nationality (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri).
Where to find it: Turkish ID card (T.C. Kimlik Kartı), passport, driving licence, and the e-Devlet (e-Government) portal.

Personal identifier name endonym: Реєстраційний номер облікової картки платника податків (РНОКПП) / “ідентифікаційний код”
Personal identifier exonym English: Registration Number of the Taxpayer Account Card (RNTRC) / Individual Tax Number
Description: Ten digits: the first five encode the number of days from 1 January 1900 to the date of birth, the next four are a serial number whose ninth digit encodes sex (odd male, even female), and the tenth is a weighted Modulus-11 check digit (weights −1,5,7,9,4,6,10,5,7).
Where to find it: Taxpayer Account Card (картка платника податків) issued by the State Tax Service of Ukraine, ID-card (паспорт громадянина України у формі ID-картки), and the Diia portal / app.

Description: Fifteen-digit number in the format 784-YYYY-XXXXXXX-C: 784 is the ISO 3166-1 numeric code for the UAE; YYYY is the year of birth; XXXXXXX is a serial; and C is a Luhn-style check digit. Issued by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP).
Where to find it: Emirates ID card carried by all citizens and residents, the ICP app, and the UAE Pass digital identity wallet.

Description: Shared NHS numbering scheme across England, Wales, and the Isle of Man: ten digits in 3-3-4 format with a Modulus-11 check digit. Scotland and Northern Ireland operate parallel schemes (CHI and H&C Number) using the same ten-digit shape.
Where to find it: NHS medical card, GP correspondence, prescriptions, hospital letters, and the NHS App.

Description: Two prefix letters, six digits, and one suffix letter (always A, B, C, or D). Example: AB123456A. The letters D, F, I, Q, U, and V are not used as either of the first two letters of the prefix; O is not used as the second letter. Administrative prefixes used internally by HMRC and DWP (OO, CR, FY, MW, NC, PP, PZ, TN) are not valid NINOs.
Where to find it: Plastic National Insurance card (legacy), letters from HMRC or DWP, payslips, form P60, tax returns, and the HMRC personal tax account.

Description: Nine-digit tax processing number issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to individuals who are required to have a U.S. taxpayer identification number but are not eligible for an SSN. Always begins with 9 and has a fourth digit in the range 50–65, 70–88, 90–92, or 94–99 (e.g. 9XX-7X-XXXX).
Where to find it: IRS notice CP565 (ITIN assignment letter), tax returns (Form 1040 and W-7 application), and W-9 / 1099 / 1042-S information returns.

Description: Nine-digit number in XXX-XX-XXXX format issued by the Social Security Administration since 1936 to track workers' earnings; randomised since 2011. Now a de facto national identifier in the United States.
Where to find it: Social Security card, W-2 forms, tax returns (IRS Form 1040), payslips, and the SSA “my Social Security” portal.

Description: Eight digits in the format X.XXX.XXX-X: seven sequential digits and a final check digit computed with weights 2,9,8,7,6,3,4 modulo 10.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad issued by the Dirección Nacional de Identificación Civil (DNIC) of the Ministry of the Interior; used for voting, banking, and government services.

Personal identifier name endonym: Shaxsiy identifikatsiya raqami (PINFL) / Шахсий идентификация рақами
Description: Fourteen digits issued by the State Personalisation Centre. The leading digit encodes century and sex (3 male / 4 female 1900–1999; 5 male / 6 female 2000–2099); the next six digits are the date of birth (YYMMDD); the remaining seven digits are a serial number including a final check digit.
Where to find it: Uzbek biometric ID-card (ID-karta), biometric passport, and the My ID app.

Description: A prefix letter (V for Venezuelan citizens, E for foreign residents) followed by up to nine digits. The base number is permanent and is reused as the Registro de Información Fiscal (RIF) tax identifier with the addition of a verification digit.
Where to find it: Cédula de Identidad Laminada issued by the Servicio Administrativo de Identificación, Migración y Extranjería (SAIME); voter rolls; RIF tax records.

Description: Twelve digits in the form PPPGYYNNNNNN: PPP is a three-digit code for the province / city of registration; G encodes sex and century of birth (0 male / 1 female born 1900s; 2 male / 3 female born 2000s; 4 male / 5 female born 2100s; etc.); YY is the last two digits of the year of birth; and NNNNNN is a random serial.
Where to find it: Căn cước công dân chip card (which replaced the older 9-digit Chứng Minh Nhân Dân, CMND), the VNeID digital identity app, and household registration (sổ hộ khẩu).

Personal identifier name endonym: 香港身份證 (Hēunggóng sānfánjing) / Hong Kong Identity Card
Description: One or two prefix letters, six digits, and a check character in parentheses (a digit 0–9 or the letter A). Example: Z123456(A). The check character is computed by mapping each letter to a number (A=10, B=11, …), multiplying by weights 9 down to 1, summing modulo 11, then taking 11 − remainder (with 10 written as A and 11 as 0).
Where to find it: Hong Kong Identity Card issued by the Immigration Department, and the “iAM Smart” mobile identity app.

Description: Nine digits, the last being a Luhn check digit computed with weights 1,2,1,2,… (sum of doubled-digit digit-sums). Stored left-padded with zeros when fewer than nine digits are recorded. Issued by the Population and Immigration Authority (רשות האוכלוסין וההגירה).
Where to find it: Israeli identity card (תעודת זהות, Teudat Zehut) including the smart biometric card, driving licence, passport (Darkon), and most government and banking services.

Personal identifier name endonym: 中华人民共和国居民身份证号码
Description: Eighteen characters in the form AAAAAA-YYYYMMDD-NNN-C: AAAAAA is the six-digit administrative-division code of the place of household registration (province, prefecture, county); YYYYMMDD is the date of birth; NNN is a three-digit serial whose final digit encodes sex (odd male, even female); and C is a check character (0–9 or X for 10) computed using the ISO 7064 MOD 11-2 algorithm.
Where to find it: 居民身份证 (Resident Identity Card) issued by the Ministry of Public Security, hukou (户口) booklet, and electronic identity wallets in apps such as WeChat and Alipay.
